info.bio:
New Birth
Formed: 1963
Styles: Funk, Disco, Quiet Storm, Smooth Soul, Soul

Group Members: James Baker, Tony Churchill, Charlie Hearndon, Robert Jackson, Austin Lander, Carl McDaniel, Robin Russell, Leroy Taylor, Londie Wiggins, Leslie Wilson, Melvin Wilson, Anne Bogan, James Baker

Biography:
Formed by Tony Churchill and music-industry veteran Harvey Fuqua, New Birth was originally named the Nite-Liters. As the Nite-Liters, they enjoyed chart action with three R&B hits: "K-Jee," "Afro-Strut," and "Pull Together.

scenes.name: Sweet funk: el soul sexual
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Tras Let’s Get It On, «Me and Mrs. Jones» de Billy Paul y «Let’s Stay Together» de Al Green llegó una nueva hornada de cantantes sensuales. Barry White, con su orquesta de estudio sobre una sección rítmica de R&B, unió la elegancia occidental y la sensualidad negra: un lujo negro impensable diez años antes. Los Moments («Sexy Mama»), Main Ingredient, los Miracles («Do It Baby»), Leon Haywood («I Want’a Do Something Freaky to You», base de «Nothin’ but a G Thang» de Dr. Dre) o New Birth mezclaron psicodelia, melodía y funk sucio; Sylvia Robinson susurró «Pillow Talk» (1973) y Major Harris remató «Love Won’t Let Me Wait» con un orgasmo simulado.

podcast.title: 17-Piece Funk Band Formation
podcast.body: New Birth was formed by the combination of the group Love Peace and Happiness and Harvey Fuqua, evolving into a large, 17-piece funk band. Anne Bogan, formerly of The Marvelettes, contributed vocals to their hit "I Can Understand It." "That group then joined with Harvey Fouqua in a 17 piece funk band called New Birth."
